coverage: Read native schematic and PCB; freshly exported connectivity confirms R1 between /IN and /OUT, C1 between /OUT and GND, and matching connector pin assignments.
Verified transient model values, stimulus, initial operating point and measurement times; decoded the supplied binary waveform and independently repeated simulation and analytical calculations.
Independently checked all five native track segments: each is 0.25 mm, meeting the 0.20 mm minimum.
Inspected native ERC and DRC reports, including ignored checks and schematic parity.
Recorded commands, versions, assumptions and outcomes in review-work/circuit/experiments/commands.json and review-work/circuit/experiments/notes.md.

findings.mechanism: R1 = 100 kΩ and C1 = 100 nF produce a 10 ms time constant. The output therefore charges too slowly to meet the required voltage at 1 ms.
findings.reasoning: For the native topology, Vout(t) = 1 − exp(−t/(R1*C1)). At 1 ms this gives 0.0951626 V, approximately 0.52484 V below the required minimum. The supplied waveform and independent simulation agree. The verification correctly represents the native circuit; its 1 ns input rise cannot explain the substantial failure margin. Passing ERC and DRC does not establish this response requirement.
findings.title: R1’s 100 kΩ value causes the 1 ms step-response requirement to fail

limitations: Tolerance, temperature, external loading, ADC sampling, EMI, parasitics and hardware behavior were not evaluated.
No manufacturer-specific component models or ratings were provided or inferred.
ERC and DRC were inspected but not rerun; their explicitly ignored checks remain untested.
Zone fill was evaluated only as saved; no refill was performed.
No falling-edge, shutdown or nonzero initial-charge tests were performed; none were required. Active reset and brownout circuitry is absent.
The 5 ms measurement has no declared acceptance bound.
